claim.summary: Under premise X of the Riesz mean formula from one premise and the strip hypothesis (0 < beta < 1 for every nontrivial zero), tau >= 2, d = |gamma - tau|, w(d) = min(2, 2/d, 4 tau/d^2), W_tau = sum over zeros of m tau^(2 beta - 1) w(d). (1) For tau^2 <= y < y' <= 2y: |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau)| <= (y/tau)(4 W_tau + 30 log 2y). (2) For an integer K >= 2 tau the zeros with d >= K contribute to W_tau at most 16 tau^2 (11 + (5/4) log 3K)/K. (3) If for all 1/2 <= sigma <= 1 and T >= 2 the zeros with beta >= sigma and |gamma| <= T number at most M T^(2(1 - sigma)) log^a T with a >= 0, and every zero with d < tau has beta <= 1/2, then W_tau <= C_0 log^2(tau + 2) + 12 M B_a log^(a+1)(2 tau), C_0 absolute, B_a = sum 2^-i (i + 2)^a. (4) Model statement, no hypothesis: tau >= 3, L >= 42, tau L >= 180, 0 < beta <= 1, y_0 = 2^N, a = log y_0, b = a + log 2, l = 1/tau, E(z) = e^(z(b+l)) - e^(zb) - e^(za) + e^(z(a-l)), c = 2 pi/log 2, k_0 = ceil(tau L/c), k_1 >= 2 k_0 - 1, z_k = beta + i c k: |sum over k_0 <= k <= k_1 of E(z_k)/(l z_k^2)| >= 0.05 y_0^beta/L.
claim.assessment: Conditional in (1) to (3), with a complete deduction from the proof of the zero bound for the premise: each zero's term in the trapezoid carries its own exponent, and y^(beta - 1) is largest at y = tau^2; the tail by the local count; (3) by writing tau^(2 beta - 1) as an integral in sigma and summing dyadic ranges of the distance against the density hypothesis, which is unproved. (4) is elementary: on the progression the two exponentials without the ramp are aligned at y_0 and 2 y_0, the constant term of the reduced kernel adds coherently and the rotating terms are bounded by summation by parts; checked in seven cases from the four exponentials. The condition of (1) is sufficient only; (4) concerns a configuration in a model, not closed under the symmetries, and says nothing about zeta. No novelty.

claim.summary: Under premise X of the Riesz mean formula from one premise (xi entire with the nontrivial zeros as its zeros and Re xi'/xi(s) = sum m_rho (sigma - beta)/|s - rho|^2) and the strip hypothesis, classical and imported, that every nontrivial zero has 0 < beta < 1. (1) For every real t the zeros with |gamma - t| <= 1 number at most 9 + (5/4) log(|t| + 2), with multiplicity. (2) If 1/2 <= theta <= 1 and every nontrivial zero has beta <= theta, then for tau >= 2 and tau <= y < y' <= 2y: |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau)| <= C (y^theta log^2(tau + 2) + y tau^-1 log(2y)), C an absolute constant. (3) Hence for theta < 1 and y >= tau^(1/(1 - theta)) the sum is at most 8C y tau^-1 log^2 y; at theta = 1/2, the Riemann hypothesis, this is the premise of the sparse off-line exclusion with A = 2 for tau >= 2 and y >= tau^2.
claim.assessment: Conditional on premise X and the strip hypothesis, with a complete deduction: the count from the real part of xi'/xi at 2 + it and the series of the digamma function; the sum over a sharp interval compared with a trapezoid of ramps 1/tau, the edges bounded by Lambda(n) <= log n; the trapezoid as a second difference of the record's Riesz means, whose terms at a zero are bounded three ways and summed with the count. Classical in kind; not new. It shows that the conditional exclusion's premise follows from the goal from length tau^2 on; with a weaker bound on the zeros this argument gives it from a longer length, and that no shorter length is possible is not proved. The constant C is not computed. It gives no approach to the goal.

claim.summary: Notation of the Riesz mean explicit formula (R_L, D_L, F_L, X = e^L). Premise X: xi(s) = s(s-1) pi^(-s/2) Gamma(s/2) zeta(s)/2 is entire, its zeros are the nontrivial zeros rho with orders m_rho and real parts at most 1, and Re xi'/xi(s) = sum_rho m_rho (sigma - beta)/|s - rho|^2, absolutely convergent, wherever xi(s) is not 0. Under premise X alone: (0) xi'/xi(s) = C + sum_rho m_rho [1/(s - rho) - 1/(2 - rho)] and (zeta'/zeta)'(s) = 1/(s-1)^2 - sum_rho m_rho/(s - rho)^2 - sum_{q >= 1} 1/(s + 2q)^2; (1) for every L > 0 and every s other than 1, the rho and the points -2q, q >= 1: R_L(s) = -zeta'/zeta(s) + D_L(s-1) - sum_rho m_rho D_L(s-rho) - sum_{q >= 1} D_L(s+2q), the sums absolutely convergent; (2) for such s, Re R_L(s) = Re F_L(s-1) - sum_rho m_rho Re F_L(s-rho) + Re[psi(s/2 + 1)/2 - (log pi)/2] - sum_{q >= 1} Re D_L(s+2q).
claim.assessment: Conditional on one premise, with a complete elementary deduction: an entire function with constant real part is constant, which gives the partial fraction of xi'/xi and by differentiation that of (zeta'/zeta)' with absolutely convergent sums; for Re s > 1 the derivative in s of L R_L(s) is a Perron integral of (zeta'/zeta)' against X^w/w^2, which may be integrated term by term, each double pole giving the derivative of L F_L; the constant of integration vanishes as s tends to infinity, and the identity continues in s. Selberg's formula is not used. Premise X was read as a theorem statement in the density import's Lean project, which is not built here; the classical facts used beside it are the Dirichlet series of zeta'/zeta, the series of the digamma function and of its derivative.

claim.summary: W >= 0 integrable on [0, l], not almost everywhere zero, a(z) = int W(v) e^(zv) dv; beta_0, tau real, g > 0, c > 0, U > 0; points rho_j = beta_0 - c j^2/U + i(tau + j g), j an integer, unit multiplicities, so that rho_0 is strictly rightmost; P(u) = sum over all j and P_J(u) = sum over |j| <= J of a(rho_j - i tau) e^((rho_j - i tau) u). (1) For u > 0: P(u) = int W(v) e^(beta_0 x) Theta(x) dv with x = u + v and Theta(x) = sqrt(pi U/(c x)) sum over integers n of exp(-U (g x - 2 pi n)^2/(4 c x)) > 0. (2) If 0 < d <= pi, R >= 0, g x is at distance at least d from every multiple of 2 pi for U <= x <= U + R + l, and A = c (U + R + l)/U <= d^2/2, then 0 < P(u) e^(-beta_0 u)/a(beta_0) <= 4.2 A^(-1/2) e^(-d^2/(4A)) for U <= u <= U + R. (3) For J >= 1 and u >= U: |P(u) - P_J(u)| e^(-beta_0 u)/a(beta_0) <= e^(-c J^2)/(c J). (4) Hence for Lam >= 1/2, with A = d^2/(4 Lam), c = A U/(U + R + l), r = (R + l)/U and J the least integer at least sqrt(Lam/c): the 2J + 1 <= (4 Lam/d) sqrt(1 + r) + 3 points with |j| <= J, of heights within J g of tau, have |P_J(u)| e^(-beta_0 u)/a(beta_0) <= (8.4 sqrt(Lam) + 2 sqrt(1 + r)) e^(-Lam)/d on [U, U + R]. A spacing g meeting the hypothesis of (2) exists if and only if d (2 + r) <= 2 pi, and then g = d/U is one.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof: Poisson summation for a Gaussian turns the sum over the comb into a theta function whose peaks sit where g x is a multiple of 2 pi and whose width is governed by the fall of the real parts; between the peaks it is exponentially small; the points far along the comb are exponentially lower and are cut off. The construction was suggested by the reviewer of the rightmost point window criterion and is verified here with constants. Numerical control at one instance (21 points): the supremum on the window against the bound, and the direct sum against the closed form by an independent quadrature, on the window and near a peak. It is a statement about a model configuration, not about zeros of zeta: it shows that in the model a count of near-tied points of the order of the logarithm of the required accuracy suffices to hide a strictly rightmost point, so an exclusion from a bound on such sums must assume fewer; whether as many are necessary is not proved here.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Settles the open case of the rightmost point window criterion in the direction of an obstruction: near-tied points closer than the window resolves can hide a strictly rightmost point with a number of points proportional to log tau at the accuracy that Turan's premise needs, within a bounded height; so on that conditional line a hypothesis counting the near-tied off-line zeros near the height, of the order of log tau, cannot be dispensed with in the model.
significance.next_action: The lower side: the least number of points that can hide to a given accuracy, with a constant to compare with the comb's.
